 MisakaNet

mcp-name: io.github.Ikalus1988/misakanet

 The same failure, paid for twice. 
 
 Your agent hits sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked , or a gbk codec error that only
 appears on a Chinese Windows console. It has no memory of the last time — so it guesses, and the
 guesses cost turns and context. Somewhere else, another agent already paid for that exact fix.
 
 MisakaNet is where that payment is kept: a git-backed failure memory . Every lesson is a Markdown
 file in this repository — graded by evidence, reviewed like code, retrieved by an agent instead of
 guessed at.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Recorded from one real call by scripts/record hero snapshot.py and verified in CI. Not a savings claim — nothing here measures what a session would have cost. 

MCP server (8 tools) · WebMCP · llms.txt ; the local stdio server ships 11 — docs/mcp.md has both rows.

 
 Core 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Install 
   
 
 
 
 

 
 Ecosystem 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 

---

 What is MisakaNet?

 Git-backed failure memory for AI coding agents. An error shows up → the agent searches → it
applies a fix somebody already verified → if nothing matches, the miss becomes an intake, and the
intake becomes a lesson for the next agent.

Every lesson is a Markdown file: reviewed like code, graded by evidence, retrieved with BM25 over the
Python standard library. The hosted MCP endpoint adds an optional semantic fallback (bge-m3 +
Vectorize) only when BM25 returns no match; MISAKANET SEMANTIC=0 disables it. No vector database is
required locally, and no server unless you want one.

 
 --- --- 
 Lessons failure-recovery knowledge base, open and auditable under lessons/ 
 Domains rag · devops · fanuc · docker · feishu · mcp · network · ci · wsl · windows … 
 Evidence E0 intake → E1 reviewed → E2 reproduced → E3 CI verified → E4 observed reuse by two or more distinct clients 

 It is not It is 
 --- --- 
 ❌ a general memory system ✅ a failure-recovery knowledge layer 
 ❌ an agent runtime ✅ a searchable lesson database 
 ❌ a mandatory vector database / RAG stack ✅ BM25 first; optional, disable-able semantic fallback on the hosted endpoint 
 ❌ a skill marketplace ✅ debugging knowledge from real sessions 
 ❌ a general-purpose benchmark platform ✅ a corpus graded by evidence; a 267-query retrieval run is published, and the older recitation benchmark is paused 

 Install (30 seconds)

The point of an install is a first successful search , not the install. None of these needs an
account or a token.

 Your host Command 
 --- --- 
 DeepSeek Harness dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet — or type misakanet in Add plugin 
 Claude Code /plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet then /plugin install misakanet@misakanet 
 Cindy install the MisakaNet plugin (id misakanet ) from Cindy's plugin list 
 Installer-managed Claude Code · Codex · Hermes · OpenClaw · codewhale · Cursor · Gemini CLI · Copilot CLI · OpenCode · Kiro · MiniMax Code · DeepSeek Harness · Cindy 
 Any other MCP client point it at — public endpoint, anonymous reads 
 Your own code pip install misakanet-core (library) · pip install misakanet (stdio server) 

The installer-managed row is what npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup writes into each host's config.
For DeepSeek Harness that is the rules half only ( $DSH HOME/AGENTS.md ): its tools come from the
plugin in the row above, which the installer prints as the one manual step.

Updates: dsh plugin --profile web update misakanet@latest .
Installer updates: npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup@latest .
Full prerequisites and the two-package trap: How to use it.

 Your first five minutes

 1. Ask it something you have actually broken. No client installed? This curl is the whole interface:

 

 2. Read what came back. A hit returns the lesson, its evidence level , and its path — open the
file and read the fix before running any command in it. A miss returns no match plus a ready-to-call
intake: the corpus saying it does not know this one yet.

 3. Check the trust signal, not the tone. E0 – E3 say how far a lesson was verified; E4 is the
one nobody can write or vote into.

 What it answers — and what it does not

 

MisakaNet answers for the failures it has indexed, and only those. When nothing matches the reply is
 no match plus a ready-to-call intake — the corpus saying "not this one yet", not a dead end.

 Lesson vs Skill

A skill teaches an agent how to do something; a lesson records what went wrong before and how
not to fail again. MisakaNet is only the second thing. → FAQ

 Where it is today

- The numbers that move are badges , on purpose: the Lessons badge renders
 data/badges/lessons.json , regenerated by update-badges.yml , so it can lag a run but is never a
 hand-typed total.
- The top of the evidence ladder is observed, not declared. E4 needs two distinct clients
 actually retrieving a lesson, so no lesson file can carry it: the corpus declares none
 (declared distribution, regenerated and checked by CI), and the number
 that exists is the worker's daily reading of search signals , published in the
 heartbeat.
- Reported gaps arrive faster than they are triaged. The intake queue is the honest bottleneck.
- The corpus is downloadable and citable. data.misakanet.org publishes a versioned
 bundle — the full corpus, the benchmark query set, and every run artifact — with a
 per-file SHA-256 and an explicit license per file (DATASET.md). The counts
 live in each version's manifest.json , not in prose.

usage.title: How to use it
usage.html:
npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup installs MisakaNet into your assistant's own config — the same command for every client. The supported clients, and what each one gets, are in the install page. Verify an install with npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup --verify; undo it with --uninstall. Reads are anonymous and unlimited; registration is for writing (why). Node ≥ 18 for the installer, Python ≥ 3.11 for the library and stdio server.

Other channels
  • Claude Code, as a plugin — /plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet, then /plugin install misakanet@misakanet: the hosted MCP tools, no installer, no local process.
  • DeepSeek Harness — dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet: mcp__misakanet__* tools plus the session panel. The rules half (the "search before you act" block) is written by the installer into $DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md; dsh has no plugin extension point for it, so the two halves stay separate.
  • The library in your own code — pip install misakanet-core. The endpoint needs no client at all: the curl in Your first five minutes is the whole interface.
The two-package trap (it cost a real install failure, #1849)

Five packages, and two of them are both called misakanet — that reuse is the trap. Read the right-hand column, not the name:

Name What it actually is
@misaka-net/misakanet-setup (npm) the installer — a bin, no plugin entry; use it to teach an assistant to search
misakanet (npm) the DSH / Codex plugin — dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet
this repository (git) a Claude Code plugin marketplace — /plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet
misakanet (PyPI) the stdio MCP server — python3 -m misakanet.server
misakanet-core (PyPI) the library (stdlib BM25) — from misakanet.search import search_lessons
Use it as a GitHub Action

When a workflow fails, the action searches the lessons and comments the closest match on the pull request (optionally reporting the new error). Published on GitHub Marketplace.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["CI"]                # your CI workflow's name
    types: [completed]
permissions:
  actions: read                      # read the failing job's log (required)
  pull-requests: write               # post the comment
  issues: write                      # the comment endpoint is issues.createComment
jobs:
  intake:
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: Ikalus1988/MisakaNet@v1
        with:
          mode: suggest-only         # or suggest-and-intake, to report new errors too
          source: ${{ github.repository }}
